## Outcome and ownership
Child of #1357. Ensure reusable knowledge identity, permission to see it, and permission to act on it remain distinct throughout retrieval, caching, extension execution and recovery.

Reuse existing MCP principal/cache scoping, delegated authorization, context policy filters and action/recovery contracts. Relevant owners include [pm-gstv4k](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-gstv4k.toon), [pm-hv1x1x](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-hv1x1x.toon), and [pm-f05lsg](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-f05lsg.toon). #1035 already defines effect-aware recovery obligations. #1341 merged on 2026-09-28 and fixes stripped preview retry suggestions from #1337; this is a cross-surface invariant and conformance extension, not a refiling of that bug.

## Implementation plan
1. Inventory principal, scope, provenance, visibility, cache and operation-effect contracts. Define separate SDK types for stable knowledge identity, read projection policy and action authorization. Recorded authorship or model/harness attribution must not grant access.
2. Apply scope/visibility filtering before retrieval scoring, provider fan-out, shared caching and output-session reuse. Propagate bounded policy context across nested graph reads and extension providers; fail closed when a required policy cannot be applied.
3. Key caches/cursors/served-fact references by effective policy scope and revisions. Revalidate after revocation or scope changes. Ensure inaccessible data cannot leak through titles, counts, scores, existence hints, omission receipts or recovery suggestions.
4. Represent recovery effect classes explicitly. A retry may preserve or reduce the original effect/authority envelope; broader mutation, recipient, scope or target requires an explicit new action. Preview/check/plan intent survives alias normalization, SDK-to-CLI conversion, MCP adapters and package recovery.
5. Build a shared conformance suite over registered built-in/extension providers and emitted recovery envelopes. Reuse the canonical recovery implementation and add only missing coverage. Publish SDK guidance explaining local trust versus remote authority.

Illustrative names only: KnowledgeIdentity, VisibilityPolicy, ActionAuthority, RecoveryEffectEnvelope.

## Acceptance and tests
- [ ] Identical queries from disjoint scopes never cross-contaminate ranking, cached rows, references or receipts
- [ ] A high-scoring hidden item is excluded before ranking and does not create an observable identifying hint
- [ ] Read access never authorizes mutation; source/author provenance never substitutes for permission
- [ ] Revoked scope invalidates cached projections and continuation/session references
- [ ] No preview/check retry becomes mutation, including attached values, aliases, nested operations and package-defined commands
- [ ] Recovery cannot silently broaden target set, operation kind or authorization scope
- [ ] Tests cover cross-scope graphs, provider errors, invalid cursor reuse, policy updates, unsupported preview flags and adversarial provider output
- [ ] A deliberately unsafe recovery producer and a cross-scope cache negative control fail the shared gate
- [ ] SDK, CLI and MCP show equivalent policy/effect outcomes without breaking current public contracts

## Dependencies and non-goals
Provides the policy boundary for context compilation and checkpoint resume in #1357; integrate with existing authorization owners. No new identity provider or credential system, permission grants inferred from natural-language evidence, replacement of working recovery fixes, or claim of a newly reproduced security vulnerability.

## Linked implementation slices
- Supplies scope/authority/effect contracts to #1361 and #1359
- Coordinates knowledge identity with #1358 without granting authority from provenance
- Cross-scope and recovery negative controls are verified by #1362
